family: binaries, three-body systems, flybys and slingshots (families 3 and 5 of the scenario inventory)
committed: 2026-11-24, in a documentation commit that precedes tools/scenario-review.mjs, its record and its test. No run of these eleven scenarios by that runner existed when these claims and tolerances were written; the only numbers known beforehand are the planning leads quoted in the roadmap's inventory (another harness), which chose what to measure, not what passes. A claim that fails is recorded as failing with its numbers; no tolerance is widened, made conditional or made non-fatal after a run. A later change that corrects a member flips its own row in its own change.

rules.cardNumber: A number the card states is confirmed when the built world matches it within 2% of the card's value, read at t = 0 from the built bodies (masses in solar masses, distances in AU, periods in years, at the row's G).
rules.count: A count the card states is confirmed by equality at t = 0.
rules.stable: 'Stable' (or a card that promises an orbit is kept) means no body is lost, merged or ejected over the run unless the card says so.
rules.pattern: A pattern claim (gains speed, walks outward, comes apart) is judged by the measure written in its own line, never by eye.
rules.rates: Each member runs from its own row (its sim_speed and max_timestep, its integrator) for the time in its line, once at 30, 60 and 120 frames a second, stepped the way the page steps it (js/timestep.js frameAdvance, then substepPlan, one updatePhysics per piece). A claim holds only when it holds at all three.
rules.seeds: A member whose world is generated (a random population) runs under seed 'audit' and under seed 'audit-2'; a claim about an event holds only when the event occurs under both. A member whose world is fully written down runs under seed 1.
rules.stepsPerPeriod: The fastest body watched completes at most one period per 200 steps of the row's step at 60 frames a second (the step the page takes at the row's speed and cap); fewer than 200 steps per period is recorded as a finding for the member's speed and cap, not as a pass.
rules.verdicts: KEEP (every claim within tolerance; ledger REVIEWED CLEAR), REFRAME (the claim is the wrong thing: card text in both languages, zoom, speed or cap; ledger REVISED in its own change), CORRECT (the world is the wrong thing: initial conditions, population, generator rule or settings for this row only; ledger REVISED in its own change). The strongest members stay unless a run contradicts a claim.
rules.notRun: A check this runner cannot make (the scene at 1366x800 and 375x812, the event within 60 s of play in a browser) is recorded NOT RUN with the reason, never inferred.
